newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN METALS-COPPER PRICES SEEN STEADY.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN METALS-COPPER PRICES SEEN STEADY.

text.p: A decision by India's southern state of Tamil Nadu to allow Sterlite Industries Ltd to re-open its copper smelter may not have much impact on the metal's price in the local market, traders said.
"There's no shortage of copper in the market," Sharad Parikh, president of the Bombay Metal Exchange, told Reuters by telephone. "It's mainly because there has been hardly any demand for the metal."

The state government's decision followed a report by a committee of environmental and medical experts which cleared Sterlite of the charge that its copper smelter was behind a suspected gas leak in July.

In the week to Wednesday, copper lost 100 rupees to 13,100 rupees per quintal on the Bombay market. Imported copper was quoted at around 13,100/13,200 rupees per quintal following a downtrend on the London Metal Market (LME).
Aluminium, quoted at 7,800 rupees per quintal, is expected to remain steady in the current week.
Traders said domestic aluminium producers had resisted the temptation to raise prices in a bid to stoke demand.
India imports most of its non-ferrous metals except aluminium, and local prices move in line with the LME trend.

Zinc has remained steady at 8,400 rupees per quintal after its recent surge when industrial users bought the metal fearing a price hike by the local monopoly, the state-owned Hindustan Zinc Ltd (HZL).
Traders said HZL had raised its zinc prices by 200 rupees per quintal against the 600 expected by industrial users.
Nickel and tin dropped 1,000 rupees and 500 rupees to 33,100 rupees and 28,700 rupees per quintal respectively.
"The market is expected to be very quiet in the next few days," Parikh added.
